identity.title: Root Cause Analysis of Anomalies in Multivariate Time Series through Granger Causal Discovery

problem.claim: Identifying anomaly root causes in multivariate time series is difficult because the series have complex dependencies.

contributions.claim: Introduces AERCA, which integrates Granger causal discovery with root cause analysis.
Defines anomalies as interventions on exogenous variables, learns Granger causality, and models exogenous-variable distributions under normal conditions.
Identifies root causes by highlighting exogenous variables that significantly deviate from their normal states.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish AERCA as a comprehensive approach that inherently integrates Granger causal discovery and root cause analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on multiple synthetic and real-world datasets show AERCA accurately captures causal relationships and effectively identifies anomaly root causes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex dependencies make anomaly root-cause identification challenging.
AERCA integrates Granger causal discovery with root-cause analysis and treats anomalies as interventions on exogenous variables.
The method models normal exogenous-variable distributions and flags significant deviations as root causes.
Experiments across synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to support causal capture and root-cause identification.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links its anomaly definition, normal-state distribution model, and root-cause criterion into one explicit pipeline.

lessons.interpretation: A tightly specified chain from problem definition to decision rule can make a proposed method's intended reasoning easier to assess.
lessons.application: Define the target phenomenon operationally, state the reference distribution or baseline, and connect deviations from it to the final decision.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when anomalies cannot reasonably be represented as interventions on exogenous variables.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
It does not state a limitation of existing approaches, so the research gap cannot be extracted.
The causal and root-cause claims are author-reported; proof details and implementation specifics are not provided.
